elements.element: The aggregate liability cap applies mutually to both Parties.
elements.evidence: Section 7(b) limits “each Party's total aggregate liability,” making the cap mutual.

elements.element: The fee-based limb of the cap includes fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim.
elements.evidence: Section 7(b) expressly uses “the fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim.”

elements.element: The cap equals the greater of the 12-month fee-based limb and USD 1,000,000.
elements.evidence: Section 7(b) sets the cap at “the greater of” the specified 12-month fees and USD 1,000,000.

elements.element: Indirect damages are excluded on a mutual basis.
elements.evidence: Section 7(a) provides that “NEITHER PARTY” is liable for indirect damages, subject to symmetrically drafted exceptions.

elements.element: Consequential damages are excluded on a mutual basis.
elements.evidence: Section 7(a) provides that “NEITHER PARTY” is liable for consequential damages, subject to symmetrically drafted exceptions.

elements.element: Liability for breach of confidentiality obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: Breach of a Party's confidentiality obligations is an Excluded Claim and therefore outside the cap in Section 7(b).

elements.element: Liability for breach of data protection obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: Breach of a Party's data protection obligations is expressly included in Excluded Claims.

elements.element: Liability for breach of security obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: Breach of a Party's security obligations is expressly included in Excluded Claims.

elements.element: Liability for indemnification obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: A Party's indemnification obligations are expressly included in Excluded Claims.

elements.element: Liability for gross negligence is uncapped.
elements.evidence: A Party's gross negligence is expressly included in Excluded Claims.

elements.element: Liability for wilful misconduct is uncapped.
elements.evidence: A Party's wilful misconduct is expressly included in Excluded Claims.

elements.element: Liability for fraud is uncapped.
elements.evidence: A Party's fraud is expressly included in Excluded Claims.

elements.element: Liability for infringement of the other Party's intellectual property rights is uncapped.
elements.evidence: A Party's infringement of the other Party's intellectual property rights is expressly included in Excluded Claims.

elements.element: Customer's payment obligations are not treated as damages for purposes of the liability cap.
elements.evidence: Section 7(b) expressly states that Customer's payment obligations are not damages for purposes of the cap.

elements.element: The liability cap applies mutually to both Parties.
elements.evidence: Section 7(b) applies the cap to “each Party's total aggregate liability.”

elements.element: The cap amount is 12 months' fees.
elements.evidence: The cap is the greater of 12 months' fees and USD 1,000,000, so it can exceed 12 months' fees; the fallback amount is not unconditionally implemented.

elements.element: Liability for indemnification obligations is carved out of the cap.
elements.evidence: Indemnification obligations are expressly included in Excluded Claims.

elements.element: Liability for breach of confidentiality obligations is carved out of the cap.
elements.evidence: Breach of confidentiality obligations is expressly included in Excluded Claims.

elements.element: Liability for gross negligence is carved out of the cap.
elements.evidence: Gross negligence is expressly included in Excluded Claims.

elements.element: Liability for wilful misconduct is carved out of the cap.
elements.evidence: Wilful misconduct is expressly included in Excluded Claims.

result.reason: The operative addition implements every preferred requirement: a mutual aggregate cap using the greater-of formula, the requested uncapped categories, and the payment-obligation clarification, while Section 7(a) retains a mutual indirect/consequential-damages exclusion. The fallback is not independently satisfied because its specified cap is 12 months' fees, whereas the rendered cap may be higher due to the USD 1,000,000 limb. The redline is substantively targeted and does not disturb unrelated commercial terms. Drafting is generally clear, although the preserved punctuation error (“REPRESENTATIVES„”), the use of “Excluded Claims” to encompass obligations and conduct, and the potentially ambiguous date of “the claim” slightly reduce polish.
